source_text:
2.5 Χρίσμα βελῶν Χρίουσι Σκύθαι βέλη τὸ καλούμενον «τοξικὸν» πρὸς
ταχεῖαν ἀναίρεσιν τῶν τιτρωσκομένων. Ζητοῦντι δέ μοι τοῦτο ἀνήρ τις ἀξιόχρεος
δέδωκε τὸ ὑποτεταγμένον φάρμακον, τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνέργειαν ἀποτελοῦν· ἔστι δὲ
τοῦτο· τιθύμαλλον τὴν χαρακίτην ἥτις ἄνεισιν εἰς κλάδους καυλώδεις, ταύτην
λαβών, βάλε εἰς ἄγγος νεουργὲς ὀστράκινον καὶ καῦσον μετ' ὕδατος μέχρις οὗ πᾶσαν
ἑαυτῆς τὴν πιμελὴν τῷ θερμῷ ἐναφήσει ὕδατι· εἶτα τὰ ἐμβληθέντα τῆς βοτάνης
ξύλα ἀναγαγών, ἕτερα χλωρὰ ἔμβαλε τῷ αὐτῷ ὕδατι· πάλιν ἀνάγαγε καί, βαλὼν
ἄλλα, καῦσον μέχρις οὗ τὸ ὕδωρ ἐκ τοῦ τούτων ὀποῦ γένηται μελιτῶδες. Ἐγὼ δὲ εἰ
πεποίηται ἀσφαλῶς οὐ θαρρῶ. Φασὶ δέ τινες τῶν ἀρχαίων ὅτι καὶ τοῦ ἔχεως ἰὸς καὶ
ἀσπίδος σαλαμάνδρας τε εἰς τοῦτο ἀπαράβατος.
pass_a_gloss: 2.5 Anointing of-arrows. Anoint Scythians arrows the called toxicon toward swift killing of-the-being-wounded. To-me-seeking but this a-man some trustworthy gave the below-set-out drug, the same activity producing; it-is but this: spurge the palisade-kind which rises into branches stalk-like, this having-taken, throw into vessel newly-made earthen and boil with water until all of-itself the fat to-the hot it-will-release water; then the having-been-put-in of-the-plant woods having-drawn-up, other green throw into-the same water; again draw-up and, having-thrown others, boil until the water from the of-these juice becomes honey-like. I but if it-has-been-made safely not I-am-confident. Say but some of-the ancients that also of-the-viper venom and of-asp of-salamander both into this unfailing.
pass_b_english: Anointing of arrows. Scythians anoint arrows with the so-called toxicon for the swift killing of those they wound. When I was seeking this, a trustworthy man gave me the drug set out below, which produces the same effect.

It is this: take the palisade-spurge, which rises into stalk-like branches; put it into a newly made earthen vessel and boil it with water until it releases all its fat into the hot water. Then draw up the woods of the plant that were put in, and throw other green ones into the same water. Draw them up again and, throwing in others, boil until the water from their juice becomes honey-like. I do not have confidence whether this has been made safely. Some of the ancients say that the venom of the viper, and of the asp and the salamander as well, is unfailing for this.

choices.why: Botanical: the spurge that rises into stalk-like branches (Dioscorides χαρακίας). Not 'lay wool'.
Arrow-poison the Scythians smear on shafts; not a generic toxin-word.
Unused terracotta for the boil. ὀστράκινον is earthenware, not oyster-like.

choices.term: τοῦ ἔχεως ἰὸς καὶ ἀσπίδος σαλαμάνδρας τε
choices.english: venom of the viper and of the asp and of the salamander
choices.why: Poison-context: ἔχις is viper, ἀσπίς the asp (not a shield), salamander a third venom.
rejected: scorpion venom and the salamander's shield

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
